entries.note: The carrier accepted the load tender; a truckload's carrier sends it several times before the pickup.
The driver is at the shipper; the freight is not on board yet.
A truckload carrier's spelling of the code.
The tracking page dates its pickup step by this wording.
At the delivering terminal, before a delivery is booked; later rows show the freight still moving.
The adapter adds the row's late reason, as in SHIPMENT DELAYED: TRAP FOR CUSTOMER.
Handed to another carrier, not to the consignee; XPO sends it beside its tender for delivery.
The truck is at the consignee; carriers send it beside, before or after the unloading of the same minute.
The tracking page dates its delivered step by this code.
The tracking page's script reads it as out for delivery when the row's state is the consignee's; the adapter stages it in transit elsewhere, so the code alone gets no stage.
A forecast dated on the estimated day, often at midnight: the adapter reads it as the estimate when the tracking record gives none, never as a scan.
The booked delivery slot, without a place: the adapter reads it as the estimate when the tracking record gives none, never as a scan.
